title: Taiwan Plans Its Own Rare-Earth Plant to Protect Key Industries
summaryZh: 工研院擬建稀土示範廠，2030年底前可供應台灣一半需求。
summaryHi: ताइवान का ITRI दुर्लभ मृदा संयंत्र बनाएगा, जो 2030 तक देश की आधी ज़रूरत पूरी कर सकता है।
summaryEs: El ITRI de Taiwán planea una planta de tierras raras que cubriría la mitad de la demanda en 2030.
summaryJa: 工業技術研究院がレアアース実証工場を計画、2030年末に国内需要の半分を賄う。
summaryKo: 대만 공업기술연구원, 2030년까지 수요 절반 충당할 희토류 시범공장 추진.
summaryEn: Taiwan's ITRI plans a rare-earth plant that could supply half of the island's needs by the end of 2030.
paragraphs: Taiwan's Industrial Technology Research Institute (ITRI) is planning a rare-earth demonstration plant that could supply half of the island's demand by the end of 2030, ITRI President Chang Pei-zen said on Saturday.

The plan comes as Chinese export controls on rare earths raise concerns about the security of industrial supply chains. Even when these metals do not appear in finished products, they are found in the magnets used in factory machinery, including the automated equipment in chip plants. Reuters has reported that TSMC is looking for alternatives to such components, although the company did not comment.

The facility would produce 500 metric tons a year, a hundredfold increase on ITRI's existing experimental line, which makes about 5,000 kilograms annually. Construction is expected to be completed by the end of 2028, after which engineers will fine-tune the process to reach full output.

ITRI hopes to locate the plant in an industrial park so that it can be transferred to a private operator more easily. Funding would have to come from the National Science and Technology Council, and commercial terms, such as possible government price guarantees for investors, are still being negotiated.

Chang noted that although Taiwan's demand is relatively small, the materials are indispensable. Separating them is technically challenging because the elements have very similar properties, and the process can involve hundreds or even thousands of stages.
Rare earths are special metals. Factories need them to make magnets, machines and chips. Taiwan buys most of them from other countries.
China now has strict rules on selling rare earths. This worries Taiwan, because its factories need these metals every day.
A big research group in Taiwan, called ITRI, has a plan. It wants to build a new plant that makes 500 tonnes of rare earths a year. That is about half of what Taiwan needs.
The building should be ready at the end of 2028. The team then wants it to work well by the end of 2030. Later, a private company may run it.
The work is not easy. The metals are very similar, so it is hard to separate them.

Taiwan's Industrial Technology Research Institute (ITRI) wants to build a rare-earth plant that could meet half of the island's needs by the end of 2030, its president, Chang Pei-zen, said on Saturday.

Rare earths are a group of metals used in magnets and many machines, including the equipment inside chip factories. China has recently put controls on their export, and Taiwanese companies are worried about their supply.
The new plant would produce 500 tonnes a year. ITRI's current test line makes only about 5,000 kilograms a year, so the new site would be 100 times bigger. Building should finish by the end of 2028.

ITRI wants to put the plant in an industrial park so that it can later be handed to a private company. The government's science council would need to pay for it, and officials are still discussing whether to promise investors a minimum price.
Chang said Taiwan does not need a large amount of rare earths, but it cannot do without them. He added that separating them is very difficult because the elements are so alike.

Taiwan's Industrial Technology Research Institute (ITRI) is planning a rare-earth demonstration plant that could supply half of the island's demand by the end of 2030, ITRI President Chang Pei-zen said on Saturday.

The plan comes as Chinese export controls on rare earths raise concerns about the security of industrial supply chains. Even when these metals do not appear in finished products, they are found in the magnets used in factory machinery, including the automated equipment in chip plants. Reuters has reported that TSMC is looking for alternatives to such components, although the company did not comment.

The facility would produce 500 metric tons a year, a hundredfold increase on ITRI's existing experimental line, which makes about 5,000 kilograms annually. Construction is expected to be completed by the end of 2028, after which engineers will fine-tune the process to reach full output.

ITRI hopes to locate the plant in an industrial park so that it can be transferred to a private operator more easily. Funding would have to come from the National Science and Technology Council, and commercial terms, such as possible government price guarantees for investors, are still being negotiated.

Chang noted that although Taiwan's demand is relatively small, the materials are indispensable. Separating them is technically challenging because the elements have very similar properties, and the process can involve hundreds or even thousands of stages.

Taiwan's leading applied research body, the Industrial Technology Research Institute (ITRI), has unveiled plans for a rare-earth demonstration plant capable of meeting half of the island's demand by the end of 2030, according to its president, Chang Pei-zen.

The initiative reflects growing unease over Beijing's export restrictions, which have exposed how dependent manufacturers are on a handful of suppliers. Rare earths may be absent from finished goods, yet the magnets that drive industrial machinery, including the highly automated tools in semiconductor fabs, rely on them. Reuters has reported that TSMC is exploring substitutes for such parts, though the chipmaker declined to comment.

With an annual capacity of 500 metric tons, the plant would represent a hundredfold scale-up from ITRI's pilot line, which currently turns out roughly 5,000 kilograms a year. Construction is slated for completion by late 2028, leaving two years to refine the process.

ITRI intends to situate the facility in an industrial park to ease its eventual handover to a private operator. The National Science and Technology Council would have to earmark the funding, while incentives such as state price guarantees for investors remain under discussion.

Chang acknowledged that Taiwan's consumption is modest but stressed that the materials are indispensable. Because the elements share almost identical properties, separating them is notoriously difficult and may require hundreds or even thousands of processing stages.

In a move aimed at reducing strategic vulnerability, Taiwan's Industrial Technology Research Institute (ITRI) has announced plans for a rare-earth demonstration plant that could satisfy half of domestic demand by the close of 2030, its president, Chang Pei-zen, revealed.

The proposal is a direct response to Chinese export controls, which have prompted concern about the resilience of the island's industrial supply chains. Although rare earths seldom feature in finished products, they are essential to the magnets in factory machinery, notably the automated systems in advanced chip plants. TSMC is reportedly investigating alternatives to these components, although it has not commented publicly.

The planned plant would yield 500 metric tons annually, a hundredfold expansion of ITRI's experimental line, which produces approximately 5,000 kilograms a year. Construction is scheduled to conclude by the end of 2028, followed by a period of process optimisation.

Crucially, ITRI envisages locating the site in an industrial park to facilitate a subsequent transfer to the private sector. Its funding would depend on the National Science and Technology Council, and the commercial framework, including potential government price guarantees to attract investors, has yet to be finalised.

Chang conceded that Taiwan's requirements are comparatively small, yet he emphasised that the materials are indispensable. Since the elements possess remarkably similar properties, separation is technically demanding and can entail hundreds or even thousands of stages.

parts.ex: The main parts of the house are built.

pay.ex: The government will pay for the new hospital.

pei-zen.en: part of the name of ITRI's president, Chang Pei-zen

period.ex: The museum is closed for a short period.

pilot.en: done as a small test first
pilot.ex: The pilot projects start next year.

planned.ex: The planned trip was cancelled because of rain.

planning.en: deciding to do something in future
planning.ex: The EU is planning new rules.

plans.ex: The town has plans for a new park.

plants.ex: The town has two power plants.

possess.en: to have a quality or skill
possess.ex: Few people possess her talent for languages.

potential.ex: We discussed potential problems with the plan.

president.en: the elected head of a country

price.en: the money you pay for something
price.ex: The price of bread went up.

private.en: not owned or run by the government
private.ex: She works for a private company.

process.en: a series of steps to reach a result
process.ex: The hiring process took two months.

processing.en: doing a series of actions on data or materials

produce.ex: The farm produces rice and tea.

produces.ex: This farm produces milk and cheese.

promise.en: to say you will surely do something
promise.ex: I promise to call you tomorrow.

prompted.ex: The storm prompted the school to close early.

properties.en: the special qualities of a substance

publicly.ex: The results will be publicly available soon.

put.ex: They put the new office in the city centre.

raise.en: to cause people to have a feeling or worry
raise.ex: The price rise raised fears among shoppers.

rare.ex: We saw a rare bird on the island.

rare-earth.en: relating to rare earths, a group of special metals

reach.en: to get to a certain level
reach.ex: Prices could reach a new high.

ready.en: finished and able to be used

reducing.ex: We are reducing plastic in our shop.

refine.en: to improve something by making small changes
refine.ex: We need to refine our plan before we start.

reflects.en: shows or is caused by something

relatively.ex: The test was relatively easy for most students.

remain.en: to stay in the same state

reported.en: told people about news in the media
reported.ex: The newspaper reported the story on Monday.

reportedly.en: according to what people say or report
reportedly.ex: The deal is reportedly worth millions.
reportedly.ja: 伝えられるところでは

represent.ex: Sales to Russia represent half its trade.

requirements.en: things that are needed or demanded
requirements.ex: The job has strict entry requirements.

research.ex: Research shows that exercise helps sleep.

resilience.en: the ability to keep working through problems
resilience.ex: The new walls improve the city's resilience to floods.

note.meaning: 韌性；系統受衝擊後維持或恢復的能力。文中指供應鏈的抗風險能力。
note.usage: 常用 supply chain resilience、resilience to sth；形容詞 resilient。

example.en: Firms are trying to build resilience into their supply chains.
example.zh: 企業正努力提升供應鏈的韌性。

noteEn.meaning: the ability to deal with problems and recover quickly.
noteEn.usage: Often 'the resilience of supply chains', 'build resilience'.

noteHi.meaning: मुश्किलों को सहने और जल्दी उबरने की क्षमता।
noteHi.usage: supply chain resilience, build resilience आम हैं।
noteHi.exampleTr: कंपनियाँ अपनी आपूर्ति शृंखला को मज़बूत बनाने की कोशिश कर रही हैं।

noteEs.meaning: capacidad de resistir problemas y recuperarse.
noteEs.usage: Se dice supply chain resilience, build resilience.
noteEs.exampleTr: Las empresas intentan reforzar la resiliencia de sus cadenas de suministro.

noteJa.meaning: 困難に耐え素早く回復する力；強靭性。
noteJa.usage: supply chain resilience、build resilience の形が多い。
noteJa.exampleTr: 企業はサプライチェーンの強靭性を高めようとしている。

noteKo.meaning: 어려움을 견디고 빨리 회복하는 능력; 회복력.
noteKo.usage: supply chain resilience, build resilience 형태가 흔하다.
noteKo.exampleTr: 기업들은 공급망의 회복력을 높이려 하고 있다.

response.ex: The film got a warm response from critics.

restrictions.en: rules that limit what people can do

revealed.ex: The report revealed a big drop in sales.

rules.en: official instructions about what is allowed
rules.ex: The school has strict rules about phones.

said.ex: She said the shop was closed.

satisfy.en: to meet a need or standard
satisfy.ex: The new rules satisfy most parents.

scale-up.en: an increase in the size of a process or business
scale-up.ex: The scale-up will create two hundred jobs.

scheduled.ex: The meeting is scheduled for Monday.

science.ex: She has loved science since she was a child.

sector.en: a part of a country's economy
sector.ex: The public sector employs many nurses.

security.ex: Energy security is a top priority.

seldom.ex: He seldom eats breakfast at home.

selling.ex: The shop started selling coffee last year.

semiconductor.en: material used to make computer chips
semiconductor.ex: Taiwan has a large semiconductor industry.

separate.en: to divide things that are mixed together
separate.ex: It is hard to separate the metals.

separating.en: dividing things that are mixed together
separating.ex: Separating the waste makes recycling easier.

separation.en: the process of dividing things that are mixed
separation.ex: The separation of metals needs special equipment.

share.en: to have the same feature as something else
share.ex: The two cities share a long history.

similar.ex: My bag is similar to yours.

site.en: the place where a building or work is

situate.en: to build or put something in a particular place
situate.ex: They want to situate the school near the park.

slated.en: planned to happen at a certain time
slated.ex: The bridge is slated to open next spring.

small.ex: It's a small town in the west.

so.ex: It was raining, so we stayed home.

special.ex: He is a special adviser to the minister.

stages.en: steps or points in a process

state.en: provided or controlled by the government
state.ex: The project depends on state funding.

still.ex: She is still waiting for the bus.

strategic.en: related to long-term plans and big goals

stressed.ex: She stressed the need for action.

strict.ex: The school has strict rules about phones.

note.meaning: 隨後的；後續的。文中指工廠建成之後再移轉給民間。
note.usage: 放在名詞前（a subsequent transfer）；subsequent to = after（正式）；副詞 subsequently。

example.en: Subsequent tests confirmed the first results.
example.zh: 後續的測試證實了最初的結果。

noteEn.usage: Used before a noun: 'a subsequent transfer', 'in subsequent years'.

noteHi.usage: संज्ञा से पहले: a subsequent transfer; subsequent to = after।
noteHi.exampleTr: बाद के परीक्षणों ने पहले नतीजों की पुष्टि की।

noteEs.usage: Va antes del sustantivo: a subsequent transfer.
noteEs.exampleTr: Las pruebas posteriores confirmaron los primeros resultados.

noteJa.usage: 名詞の前に置く：a subsequent transfer。
noteJa.exampleTr: その後の試験で最初の結果が確認された。

substitutes.en: things used instead of something else

suppliers.ex: The shop works with local suppliers.

supply.ex: The supply of fresh water is limited.

systems.en: sets of connected parts that work together
systems.ex: The city upgraded its water systems.

taiwan.en: an island country in East Asia

technically.en: in a way that involves skill or technology
technically.ex: The project is technically difficult but possible.

technology.en: machines and science used in practice

terms.ex: Both sides agreed on the terms of the deal.

test.ex: The car went on a test drive.

then.ex: First read the text, then answer the questions.

these.en: the ones here or just mentioned

thousands.en: many thousands; a very large number
thousands.ex: Thousands of birds fly south each year.

times.en: used to say how much bigger something is
times.ex: The new house is three times bigger.

tonnes.ex: The truck carried ten tonnes of sand.

tons.en: units of weight (a metric ton is 1,000 kg)
tons.ex: The truck carries ten tons of rice.

tools.en: things used to do a job
tools.ex: Put the kitchen tools in the drawer.

transfer.en: moving something from one owner to another
transfer.ex: The transfer of the company took six months.

transferred.en: moved from one place to another
transferred.ex: The money was transferred to his account.

turns.ex: The factory turns out 500 cars a week.

under.en: under the arrangement: by the deal; under way: happening
under.ex: Under the deal, each side pays half.

note.meaning: 不安；憂慮。文中指對中國出口管制的擔憂。
note.usage: 不可數名詞；growing unease over/about sth；形容詞 uneasy。

example.en: There is growing unease over rising food prices.
example.zh: 人們對食品價格上漲日益感到不安。

noteEn.meaning: a feeling of worry that something is wrong.

noteHi.exampleTr: खाने की बढ़ती कीमतों को लेकर बेचैनी बढ़ रही है।

noteEs.exampleTr: Crece la inquietud por la subida de los precios de los alimentos.

noteJa.meaning: 何かがおかしいという不安感。
noteJa.exampleTr: 食品価格の上昇に不安が広がっている。

noteKo.exampleTr: 식품 가격 상승에 대한 불안이 커지고 있다.

unveiled.ex: The company unveiled a new phone.

used.en: put into service for a purpose
used.ex: The old bricks were used again.

vulnerability.en: the state of being easily harmed
vulnerability.ex: The flood showed the town's vulnerability to storms.

note.meaning: 脆弱性；容易受到傷害或衝擊。文中指台灣過度依賴進口稀土的風險。
note.usage: 常見 vulnerability to sth、strategic vulnerability；形容詞 vulnerable。

example.en: The shortage exposed the country's vulnerability to supply shocks.
example.zh: 這次短缺暴露了該國易受供應衝擊的弱點。

noteEn.meaning: the state of being easily harmed or affected.

noteHi.meaning: आसानी से नुकसान झेलने की स्थिति; कमज़ोरी।
noteHi.usage: vulnerability to sth आम है; विशेषण vulnerable।
noteHi.exampleTr: इस कमी ने आपूर्ति झटकों के प्रति देश की कमज़ोरी उजागर कर दी।

noteEs.meaning: estado de ser fácilmente dañado; vulnerabilidad.
noteEs.usage: Se usa vulnerability to algo; adjetivo vulnerable.
noteEs.exampleTr: La escasez mostró la vulnerabilidad del país ante crisis de suministro.

noteJa.usage: vulnerability to 〜 の形が多い。形容詞は vulnerable。
noteJa.exampleTr: その不足は供給ショックに対する国の脆弱性を露呈した。

noteKo.usage: vulnerability to ~ 형태가 흔하다. 형용사는 vulnerable.
noteKo.exampleTr: 그 부족 사태는 공급 충격에 대한 나라의 취약성을 드러냈다.

wants.ex: She wants a quiet place to study.

whether.en: used to express a choice (if or not)

will.en: used to talk about the future
will.ex: The new bridge will open next year.

worried.ex: She is worried about her exam.

worries.ex: Money is one of his biggest worries.

would.ex: A new park would help the town.

yet.ex: The cost is not yet known.

yield.ex: Each tree can yield fifty apples.
